what: Drives a Lottie bound to scroll — first frame when the element’s top edge reaches the bottom of the screen, last frame when its bottom edge leaves the top of the screen, linear proportion in between (frame = round(progress × total frames)), so the keyframe curve inside the Lottie becomes the scroll curve as is. It listens to scroll only while visible (Studio Lottie’s ‹scroll› playback). It suits scenes where a yellow light turns fully on from 0 (frames 9→34, size 0→1) or where two lights enter from both sides and brighten as they overlap (frames 29→59, position and opacity). With mode: fixed, since it sits in a fixed panel, when the element does not move it goes 0→end→0 every span px of document scroll. With look: tint, the Lottie shapes are painted in the Skin color.

options.src: Lottie JSON path (relative to the page using it) or #id — within the document <script type="application/json" id=…> Is read from (a page opened via file:// cannot load the file)
options.mode: fixed — inside a fixed panel, go back and forth every span px of document scroll (how the original Studio handles fixed elements)
options.span: mode: fixed distance (px) of a single trip, default 1000
options.rest: Frame to hold under reduced motion, default last frame
options.look: tint — fills the paths inside the Lottie with --fx-fill (default --kf-accent)
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Child element to draw the Lottie (optional) — if absent, no element at all
options.range: Only the a~b range of progress maps to the first→last frame (e.g. "0.2, 0.45"), default 0, 1 — when drawn only during one scene inside a long pinned panel

from.where: index.html .nm-about__spot (yellow light — fixed 70%×100vh plate, 1000×1000, 60 frames, size 0→1 over 9→34) · shared.js .nm-contact__spots (two lights on the contact plate — 130%×1000px, 1900×1050, 150 frames, entering from both sides over 29→59 with opacity 0→1). Original progress Kr(): (scroll bottom edge − element top) ÷ (element height + viewport height), frame round(progress/100 × total frames)

Survey charts (arc, star, box, bar, dot — 600×600·25fps·76f / 500×500·51f / 800×400·76f) in the index.html·article.html photo stage, cards and photo row — original @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web 0.71.0 setFrame(progress × totalFrames). The photo stage runs per section over top+1.5i·vh → top+(1+1.5i)·vh (the range covers the same span). Inside the site it is dotlottie-web 0.71.0 as is (shared.js OW.scrubChart)

note: The original calls the seek of dotlottie-player (built on lottie-web 5.12) directly on every scroll event. Here calls are batched once per rAF and the same frame is set with lottie-web goToAndStop. The original stays at frame 0 until the first scroll, but here it is set once after loading.
